facts: The paper presents the first application of the head-driven statistical parsing model of Collins (1999).
The head-driven statistical parsing model of Collins (1999) is applied as a simultaneous language model and parser.
The application is for large-vocabulary speech recognition.
The model is adapted to an online left to right chart-parser.
The chart-parser is for word lattices.
The parser uses structural and lexical dependencies.
Structural and lexical dependencies are not considered by n-gram models.
The parser conditions recognition on more linguistically-grounded relationships.
Experiments are on the Wall Street Journal treebank.
Experiments show word error rates competitive with the standard n-gram language model.
The experiments extract additional structural information useful for speech understanding.
